children: South Korean shares fell roughly 3% on Monday as a government pledge to deploy market stabilisation funds failed to ease concerns over the AI trade and a broader technology selloff.
was down 132.98 points, or 2.73%, at 4,736.98 by 0034 GMT, hovering at the lowest level since January.
On Sunday, authorities said they would deploy market stabilisation funds immediately if conditions worsened, after the South Korean benchmark index tumbled to a 10-month low last week.
Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution
The muted response to Seoul's policy rollout suggested investors remain more concerned about the outlook for global technology stocks than local efforts to shore up sentiment.
The sharp selloff on Monday underscores how rapidly changes in Wall Street sentiment toward AI-related spending can ripple through Asia's technology supply chain.
Investors have increasingly questioned whether massive AI investments will generate returns quickly enough to justify the costs.
The market breadth remained negative, with 810 of the 896 traded issues declining against only 68 advancers.
The benchmark bond yield held flat in early trading as investors weighed domestic policy interventions against global equity headwinds.
